# Generalised chart-export framework — test sandbox

**Goal.** Build one `exportChart(rootElement, opts)` helper that captures the **full** rendered figure — including HTML legends, captions, ranking panels, and multi-SVG facet grids — into either PNG or SVG. Then drop the existing `chartDownloadMenu` PNG path in favour of it.

**Current pain (in `obs_month_overlay.qmd`):**

- `_chartDownloadMenu_svgToPng` finds the *first* SVG inside the chartElement and serialises only that one. Multi-SVG grids (Period maps choropleth, Period polar SSP small-multiples, P2/P4 facets) export with only one cell visible.
- HTML siblings (legends, captions, ranking panels) sit *next to* the SVG, not inside it → never appear in the export.
- `chartDownloadMenu` doesn't auto-detect "composite element" vs "single SVG" — same code path for both.

**Design.** Two strategies, picked automatically by the helper:

1. **`composite-foreignObject`** (default for mixed-content / multi-SVG roots). Clone the entire `rootElement` (with computed styles inlined) into an `<svg><foreignObject>` envelope, then rasterise via `<img>` + `<canvas>` → PNG. SVG export emits the foreignObject SVG directly. Captures legends, multi-SVG grids, ranking panels, captions — anything the DOM contains.
2. **`single-svg`** (when the root IS a single SVG or contains exactly one SVG with no HTML siblings of interest). Uses the existing serialise → image → canvas path; simpler + smaller files.

**Acceptance**: the four test cases below all export PNG+SVG visibly identical to what the page shows.

```{ojs}
import { loaderDiv } from "/helpers/uiComponents.ojs";
```

## Test case 1 — single Plot.plot chart (baseline / regression check)

The simplest case. `chartDownloadMenu` already handles this. Verify the new helper produces the same output.

```{ojs}
//| label: tc1-render
tc1 = {
  const data = d3.range(0, 50).map(i => ({ x: i, y: Math.sin(i / 5) + 0.02 * i }));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 520,
    height: 280,
    title: "Single SVG — sin(x) with drift",
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "#999", strokeDasharray: "3 3" }),
      Plot.line(data, { x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#216" }),
      Plot.dot(data, { x: "x", y: "y", r: 2, fill: "#216" }),
    ],
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
exportBar({ rootElement: tc1, filename: "tc1_single_svg" })
```

## Test case 2 — multi-SVG facet grid

Multiple SVGs inside a flexbox container. Current helper captures one cell only.

```{ojs}
//| label: tc2-render
tc2 = {
  const data = d3.range(0, 50);
  const oneCell = (label, phase) => {
    const cell = Plot.plot({
      width: 200, height: 140, marginLeft: 30,
      title: label,
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "#999", strokeDasharray: "3 3" }),
        Plot.line(data.map(i => ({ x: i, y: Math.sin(i / 5 + phase) })),
                  { x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#216" }),
      ],
    });
    return cell;
  };
  return htl.html`<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 1fr);gap:8px;background:#fff;padding:8px;">
    ${oneCell("Cell 1 (phase 0)",   0)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 2 (phase π/2)", Math.PI / 2)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 3 (phase π)",   Math.PI)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 4 (phase 3π/2)", 3 * Math.PI / 2)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 5 (phase 2π)",  2 * Math.PI)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 6 (phase 5π/2)", 5 * Math.PI / 2)}
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
exportBar({ rootElement: tc2, filename: "tc2_facet_grid_6_cells" })
```

## Test case 3 — SVG + HTML legend (Period-maps-shaped)

A chart with an HTML legend below it (like Period maps' colour-ramp legend + stipple note). Current helper exports the chart SVG only; the legend goes missing.

```{ojs}
//| label: tc3-render
tc3 = {

    x: i % 20, y: Math.floor(i / 20),

  const chart = Plot.plot({
```

## Test case 4 — pure HTML (Period-table-shaped)

A heat-mapped table — no SVG anywhere. Must rasterise via foreignObject. Current helper fails entirely (no SVG → no PNG).

```{ojs}
//| label: tc4-render
tc4 = {
  const rows = ["A","B","C","D"];
  const cols = ["2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
  const cellVal = (r, c) => Math.sin((r + c) / 3) * 2;
  const shade = v => {
    const t = (v + 2) / 4;
    return `rgba(${Math.round(216 * (1 - t) + 31 * t)}, 117, ${Math.round(48 * (1 - t) + 180 * t)}, 0.6)`;
  };
  const th = "padding:6px 12px;background:#f3f3f3;border-bottom:2px solid #888;font-size:0.85em;text-align:center;";
  const td = "padding:6px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #eee;font-size:0.9em;text-align:center;";
  return htl.html`<div style="background:#fff;padding:8px;">
    <p style="margin:0 0 6px;font-weight:600;color:#222;">Test 4: pure HTML heat-mapped table</p>
    <table style="border-collapse:collapse;">
      <thead><tr><th style="${th}">Row</th>${cols.map(c => htl.html`<th style="${th}">${c}</th>`)}</tr></thead>
      <tbody>${rows.map((r, ri) => htl.html`<tr>
        <td style="${td};font-weight:600;background:#f6f6f6;">${r}</td>
        ${cols.map((c, ci) => {
          const v = cellVal(ri, ci);
          return htl.html`<td style="${td};background:${shade(v)};">${(v >= 0 ? "+" : "") + v.toFixed(2)}</td>`;
        })}
      </tr>`)}</tbody>
    </table>
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
// Pass tc4's row-major data so the CSV menu item is enabled.
exportBar({
  rootElement: tc4,
  filename: "tc4_pure_html_table",
  data: (() => {
    const rows = ["A","B","C","D"];
    const cols = ["2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
    return rows.flatMap((r, ri) =>
      cols.map((c, ci) => ({ row: r, period: c, value: Math.sin((ri + ci) / 3) * 2 })));
  })(),
})
```

## Test case 5 — SVG composite with d3 (polar-clock-shaped)

A single SVG, but containing multiple `<g>` subgraphs at calculated positions — mimics Period polar's grid-inside-one-SVG layout.

```{ojs}
//| label: tc5-render
tc5 = {
  const cellW = 200, cellH = 200, nCols = 3, nRows = 2;
  const totalW = cellW * nCols + 30, totalH = cellH * nRows + 50;
  const svg = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${totalW} ${totalH}`)
    .attr("width", totalW).attr("height", totalH)
    .style("font-family", "system-ui, sans-serif")
    .style("background", "#fff");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", totalW / 2).attr("y", 16)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 600)
    .text("Test 5: 6-cell SVG composite (one root SVG, multiple <g> subgraphs)");
  for (let r = 0; r < nRows; r++) for (let c = 0; c < nCols; c++) {
    const cxCell = 15 + c * cellW + cellW / 2;
    const cyCell = 30 + r * cellH + cellH / 2;
    const g = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${cxCell}, ${cyCell})`);
    // Radial bars per "month" with phase per cell.
    for (let m = 0; m < 12; m++) {
      const angle = (m / 12) * 2 * Math.PI - Math.PI / 2;
      const v = 30 + 30 * Math.sin(m / 2 + r * 0.7 + c * 0.5);
      g.append("line")
        .attr("x1", 0).attr("y1", 0)
        .attr("x2", Math.cos(angle) * v).attr("y2", Math.sin(angle) * v)
        .attr("stroke", d3.interpolateInferno(0.2 + 0.7 * (m / 11)))
        .attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
    }
    g.append("text").attr("y", -75).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
      .attr("font-size", 10).attr("font-weight", 600).text(`Cell ${r * nCols + c + 1}`);
  }
  return svg.node();
}
```

```{ojs}
exportBar({ rootElement: tc5, filename: "tc5_single_svg_composite" })
```

## The helper (v2 — html-to-image rasteriser)

v1 used a DIY `<svg><foreignObject>` envelope. Three failure modes in
the wild (Pete 2026-06-05 test run):
- Plot.plot output is a `<figure>` containing `<svg>` PLUS a sibling
  `<style>` element — single-SVG serialiser dropped the sibling style,
  so the exported SVG had axes / text but no graphics.
- foreignObject with nested SVG namespace can hang the `<img>`
  rasterise step without firing `onload` OR `onerror` — PNG button
  stuck on "Rasterising…" indefinitely.
- Pure HTML rasterise via foreignObject truncated rows on TC4 (table
  missing the last row).

v2 delegates the hard problems to `html-to-image` (modern fork of
dom-to-image, MIT-licensed, ~30 KB ESM from Skypack). Better-tested
foreignObject + computed-style handling, plus an `onclone` hook that
lets us patch Plot's figure-with-style oddity before rasterise.

**Note on cell structure**: each top-level OJS binding lives in its own ```{ojs}``` fence below. Stuffing multiple bindings (`function ...`, `name = expr`) into one fence only registers the first one with the runtime — the rest are syntactically valid but never bound, and downstream cells throw `invalid binding`. This was the v2-to-v3 fix.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// html-to-image (MIT, ~30 KB ESM via esm.sh). Modern fork of dom-to-
// image; handles Plot.plot figure-with-style, multi-SVG composites,
// computed-style inlining, pixel-true bounds capture for HTML — all of
// the cases the v1 DIY foreignObject envelope choked on. esm.sh
// resolves the package's "exports" field and serves a browser-ready
// ESM bundle (Skypack 404'd in the v2 attempt).
htmlToImage = await import("https://esm.sh/html-to-image@1.11.13")
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Detect export strategy from the rootElement's shape.
//   - bare <svg>                              → single-svg
//   - <figure> with one <svg> + <style>       → plot-figure
//     (Plot.plot output — bake style into SVG then use single-svg path
//      so the export bounds = SVG bounds, not figure bounds. The
//      previous version routed Plot figures through html-to-image and
//      produced trailing whitespace because <figure>'s bounding rect
//      is wider than its inner SVG.)
//   - anything else (multi-SVG grid, HTML legend wrapper, pure HTML) →
//     composite-html2img (html-to-image library handles it).
detectExportStrategy = function(rootElement) {
  if (!rootElement) return null;
  if (rootElement.tagName?.toLowerCase() === "svg") return "single-svg";
  if (rootElement.tagName?.toLowerCase() === "figure") {
    const svgs = rootElement.querySelectorAll(":scope > svg");
    if (svgs.length === 1) return "plot-figure";
  }
  return "composite-html2img";
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Plot.plot wraps SVG inside <figure> with a sibling <style> element.
// Inline-clone that style into the SVG before serialising so class-
// based fills / strokes / fonts survive a standalone export. Idempotent.
bakePlotFigureStyles = function(rootElement) {
  if (!rootElement || rootElement.tagName?.toLowerCase() !== "figure") return rootElement;
  const svg = rootElement.querySelector(":scope > svg");
  const styles = rootElement.querySelectorAll(":scope > style");
  if (!svg || !styles.length) return rootElement;
  for (const s of styles) {
    if (svg.querySelector(":scope > style")) break;
    svg.insertBefore(s.cloneNode(true), svg.firstChild);
  }
  return rootElement;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Serialise a single SVG with xmlns + width/height set on the clone.
serialiseSingleSvg = function(svg) {
  const clone = svg.cloneNode(true);
  if (!clone.getAttribute("xmlns")) clone.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
  if (!clone.getAttribute("xmlns:xlink")) clone.setAttribute("xmlns:xlink", "http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink");
  const bbox = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
  if (!clone.getAttribute("width"))  clone.setAttribute("width",  bbox.width);
  if (!clone.getAttribute("height")) clone.setAttribute("height", bbox.height);
  return new XMLSerializer().serializeToString(clone);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Resolve the rootElement to the actual SVG to serialise for the
// single-SVG fast paths. Plot-figure: bake styles into inner SVG then
// return it. Bare SVG: return as-is. Anything else throws.
resolveSvgForExport = function(rootElement) {
  bakePlotFigureStyles(rootElement);
  if (rootElement.tagName?.toLowerCase() === "svg") return rootElement;
  if (rootElement.tagName?.toLowerCase() === "figure") {
    const inner = rootElement.querySelector(":scope > svg");
    if (inner) return inner;
  }
  const fallback = rootElement.querySelector("svg");
  if (fallback) return fallback;
  throw new Error("No SVG found in rootElement for single-svg path");
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Single-SVG fast path (PNG). No library round-trip — keeps PNG files
// small + export deterministic for the simplest case.
singleSvgPng = async function(svg, scale) {
  const dpr = scale || 2;
  const svgString = serialiseSingleSvg(svg);
  const bbox = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
  const blob = new Blob([svgString], { type: "image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const im = new Image();
    im.onload = () => {
      const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
      canvas.width  = Math.max(1, Math.round(bbox.width  * dpr));
      canvas.height = Math.max(1, Math.round(bbox.height * dpr));
      const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
      ctx.fillStyle = "#ffffff";
      ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      ctx.drawImage(im, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      canvas.toBlob(b => {
        URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
        b ? resolve(b) : reject(new Error("canvas.toBlob returned null"));
      }, "image/png");
    };
    im.onerror = e => { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); reject(new Error("Image() failed to parse single-svg payload")); };
    im.src = url;
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// PNG dispatcher.
exportChartPng = async function(opts) {
  const { rootElement, scale, strategy } = opts || {};
  const s = strategy || detectExportStrategy(rootElement);
  if (s === "single-svg" || s === "plot-figure") {
    return singleSvgPng(resolveSvgForExport(rootElement), scale);
  }
  // html-to-image: returns a Blob of PNG bytes. `pixelRatio` controls
  // dpr; `backgroundColor` forces white background so the PNG pastes
  // cleanly into docs / slides. `cacheBust` defeats stale Image cache
  // for hot-reloaded charts.
  return htmlToImage.toBlob(rootElement, {
    pixelRatio: scale || 2,
    backgroundColor: "#ffffff",
    cacheBust: true,
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// SVG dispatcher. For the composite path html-to-image emits an SVG
// data URL via toSvg → decode into a string for the download.
exportChartSvg = async function(opts) {
  const { rootElement, strategy } = opts || {};
  const s = strategy || detectExportStrategy(rootElement);
  if (s === "single-svg" || s === "plot-figure") {
    return serialiseSingleSvg(resolveSvgForExport(rootElement));
  }
  const dataUrl = await htmlToImage.toSvg(rootElement, {
    backgroundColor: "#ffffff",
    cacheBust: true,
  });
  const prefix = "data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,";
  if (dataUrl.startsWith(prefix)) return decodeURIComponent(dataUrl.slice(prefix.length));
  const b64Prefix = "data:image/svg+xml;base64,";
  if (dataUrl.startsWith(b64Prefix)) return atob(dataUrl.slice(b64Prefix.length));
  return dataUrl;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// CSV serialiser — RFC 4180-ish. Quotes fields that contain commas /
// newlines / quotes; UTF-8 BOM prefixed when written so Excel recognises
// diacritics in admin names etc.
exportDataCsv = function(opts) {
  const { data, columns } = opts || {};
  if (!Array.isArray(data) || data.length === 0) return "";
  const cols = columns ?? Object.keys(data[0]);
  const esc = v => {
    if (v == null) return "";
    const s = String(v);
    if (/[",\n\r]/.test(s)) return `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
    return s;
  };
  const header = cols.map(esc).join(",");
  const body = data.map(row => cols.map(c => esc(row[c])).join(",")).join("\n");
  return header + "\n" + body;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
triggerDownload = function(blob, filename) {
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url; a.download = filename;
  document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); document.body.removeChild(a);
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Combined Download ▾ split-button — single control offering PNG / SVG
// / CSV. The CSV menu item only enables when the caller passes a
// `data` array (or `csvColumns`). The button keeps its label as
// "Download ▾" while the dropdown lists the format choices. Click
// outside closes the menu.
exportBar = function({ rootElement, filename, data, csvColumns }) {
  const strategy = detectExportStrategy(rootElement);
  const badge = htl.html`<span style="
    font-size:10px;font-weight:700;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.05em;
    padding:2px 6px;border-radius:3px;
    background:${strategy === "composite-html2img" ? "#fff5e0" : "#e5f3ff"};
    color:${strategy === "composite-html2img" ? "#7a4f00" : "#1d3a5f"};
    border:1px solid ${strategy === "composite-html2img" ? "#f5b85e" : "#7ab4e8"};
  ">strategy: ${strategy ?? "(none)"}</span>`;

  const hasData = Array.isArray(data) && data.length > 0;

  // Style block — scoped to the wrapper.
  const styleId = `exportbar-style-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 7)}`;
  const styleEl = htl.html`<style>
    .${styleId}-row { display:flex; gap:8px; align-items:center; padding:6px 8px; border-top:1px solid #eee; background:#fafafa; margin-top:8px; }
    .${styleId}-wrap { position:relative; display:inline-block; }
    .${styleId}-btn { font-size:12px; padding:4px 10px; border:1px solid #888; border-radius:4px; background:#fff; cursor:pointer; color:#222; font-family:inherit; }
    .${styleId}-btn:hover { background:#f0f0f0; }
    .${styleId}-btn:disabled { opacity:0.5; cursor:wait; }
    .${styleId}-menu { display:none; position:absolute; top:100%; left:0; margin-top:2px; background:#fff; border:1px solid #999; border-radius:4px; box-shadow:0 4px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.18); padding:4px 0; min-width:160px; z-index:9999; }
    .${styleId}-menu.open { display:block; }
    .${styleId}-item { display:block; width:100%; padding:6px 14px; text-align:left; background:transparent; border:0; font-size:12px; color:#222; cursor:pointer; font-family:inherit; }
    .${styleId}-item:hover:not(:disabled) { background:#f0f0f0; }
    .${styleId}-item:disabled { color:#aaa; cursor:not-allowed; }
    .${styleId}-item-hint { display:inline-block; margin-left:8px; font-size:10px; color:#888; }
  </style>`;

  const btn = htl.html`<button class="${styleId}-btn">⬇ Download ▾</button>`;
  const menu = htl.html`<div class="${styleId}-menu"></div>`;
  const wrap = htl.html`<div class="${styleId}-wrap">${btn}${menu}</div>`;

  const closeMenu = () => menu.classList.remove("open");
  const openMenu  = () => menu.classList.add("open");
  btn.onclick = (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    menu.classList.toggle("open");
  };
  // Click-outside dismiss.
  const docHandler = (e) => { if (!wrap.contains(e.target)) closeMenu(); };
  document.addEventListener("click", docHandler);

  const setBusy = (label) => {
    btn.disabled = true;
    btn.textContent = label;
  };
  const setReady = () => {
    btn.disabled = false;
    btn.textContent = "⬇ Download ▾";
  };

  const pngItem = htl.html`<button class="${styleId}-item">PNG <span class="${styleId}-item-hint">raster, white bg</span></button>`;
  pngItem.onclick = async () => {
    closeMenu();
    setBusy("Rasterising…");
    try {
      const blob = await exportChartPng({ rootElement, scale: 2 });
      triggerDownload(blob, `${filename}.png`);
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("PNG export failed:", e);
      alert("PNG export failed: " + e.message);
    }
    setReady();
  };

  const svgItem = htl.html`<button class="${styleId}-item">SVG <span class="${styleId}-item-hint">vector, scalable</span></button>`;
  svgItem.onclick = async () => {
    closeMenu();
    setBusy("Serialising…");
    try {
      const svgStr = await exportChartSvg({ rootElement });
      const blob = new Blob([svgStr], { type: "image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8" });
      triggerDownload(blob, `${filename}.svg`);
    } catch (e) {
      console.error("SVG export failed:", e);
      alert("SVG export failed: " + e.message);
    }
    setReady();
  };

  const csvItem = htl.html`<button class="${styleId}-item" ${hasData ? "" : "disabled"}>CSV <span class="${styleId}-item-hint">${hasData ? `input data, ${data.length} rows` : "no input data"}</span></button>`;
  csvItem.onclick = () => {
    if (!hasData) return;
    closeMenu();
    const csv = exportDataCsv({ data, columns: csvColumns });
    // UTF-8 BOM so Excel recognises diacritics.
    const blob = new Blob(["﻿", csv], { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8" });
    triggerDownload(blob, `${filename}.csv`);
  };

  menu.append(pngItem, svgItem, csvItem);

  return htl.html`<div class="${styleId}-row">
    ${styleEl}
    ${badge}
    ${wrap}
    <span style="font-size:10px;color:#888;font-style:italic;">filename: ${filename}</span>
  </div>`;
}
```

## What to verify in the rendered page

For each of the 5 test cases:

1. **Strategy badge** —
   - TC1 (Plot.plot figure, single inner SVG) → `plot-figure` (bakes sibling `<style>` into the SVG + uses the single-svg fast path → no trailing whitespace).
   - TC2 (multi-SVG facet grid) → `composite-html2img`.
   - TC3 (SVG + HTML legend wrapper) → `composite-html2img`.
   - TC4 (pure HTML table) → `composite-html2img`.
   - TC5 (single bare SVG with `<g>` subgraphs) → `single-svg`.
2. **Click ⬇ Download ▾** — one button now. Menu items: **PNG / SVG / CSV**. CSV is enabled only when the caller passes a `data` array (TC4 here).

If any case fails: open DevTools → console; html-to-image logs verbose errors there. Paste back here.
